thread:
aisha: Hey all — first day. I'm on Windows 11 + WSL2 with the company WireGuard profile (split-tunnel). Docker pulls from registry.redwood.internal:5000 keep timing out, but public docker hub works. 'docker pull' stalls at TLS handshake. Anyone seen this? cc @infra-jen

infra-jen: welcome! usually split-tunnel + WSL routing causes that. Can you paste `ip route` from inside WSL and `wg show` from Windows? Also try `curl -v http://registry.redwood.internal:5000/v2/` from both WSL and Powershell so we know if it's DNS vs route.

aisha: quick outputs — from WSL:
```
root@DESKTOP:/home/aisha# ip route
default via 172.22.32.1 dev eth0
172.22.0.0/16 dev eth0 proto kernel scope link src 172.22.45.10
```
From Windows `wg show` (redacted keys):
```
interface: wg0
  public key: xxxxxx
  peers: 1
  latest handshake: 2m ago
  transfer: 1.2 MiB received
```
Curl from WSL: `curl: (28) Operation timed out after 300000 milliseconds`

megan: sounds like traffic to the internal subnet is still going through the default interface (WSL's virtual NIC) rather than the WireGuard one on Windows. Quick workaround: on the Windows host add a persistent route for the internal VPC CIDR pointing at the WireGuard gateway. e.g. in admin Powershell:
```
route add 10.10.0.0 mask 255.255.0.0 192.168.100.1 -p
```
(Replace with the WG gateway IP you see in `ipconfig` for the WG adapter). That usually fixes WSL since it inherits host routes.

alex: alternative: use the bastion SOCKS proxy if you need immediate registry access: `ssh -D 1080 me@bastion.redwood.internal -p 2200` then set `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` or configure Docker to use the proxy. I'll open an infra ticket so we can fix the split-tunnel config for new hires.

deploy-bot: INF-542 created: "wsl split-tunnel route inheritance / newhire" assigned to eng-infra.

aisha: added the route from megan (used the WG gateway IP) — `docker pull` now progresses. Thanks! Will leave notes on the onboarding doc about this step. :party_parrot:
